editorial.marketOverview: The latest completed US cash session remains Friday November 20: Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite -5.28% and SOX about -11%; secondary sources reported QQQ -5.67% and Nvidia -14.01%; Barron's reported VIX closing at 37.66. These are Friday reports, not new weekend observations. Severe semiconductor relative weakness and poor breadth continue to favor a bearish baseline.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the preceding 17:03 EST snapshot, the review of November 21 follow-up coverage and November 23–27 release calendars found no new verified SEC/Nvidia determination or post-Friday cash-market response. Curated Open Watch still has 174 events (updated 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00). No material change to the expected three-session path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: High volatility and chip-led selling indicate fragile risk appetite, though sharp short-covering remains plausible. Reuters' Nvidia SEC accounting inquiry report adds unresolved issuer-specific risk but is not evidence of wrongdoing. Treasury 10Y and 2Y figures from different times cannot be combined into a live curve: the older indicative 4.94% minus 4.65% equals +29 basis points only. No verified synchronized FedWatch, VXN, or maturity-matched oil prices are available.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: flash PMIs at 09:45 EST and the reopening of QQQ/SOX/SMH trading test whether semiconductor selling persists. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Analog Devices/Dell earnings are key demand checks. Wednesday November 25: clustered 08:30 macro releases and the 14:00 Beige Book may alter rates and risk appetite. Base case is unstable downside-skewed trading with possible oversold rebounds, not a certain decline.
editorial.bullCase: A coordinated rebound in QQQ, SOX and SMH, improving advance/decline breadth and lower VXN/VIX would challenge the bearish continuation thesis. Better PMIs, reassuring hardware guidance and stable yields could fuel short-covering; none of those outcomes has yet occurred.
editorial.bearCase: Renewed Nvidia governance uncertainty, continued SOX underperformance, weak breadth and elevated volatility could amplify selling if upcoming data or earnings disappoint. Friday's liquidation is confirmed retrospectively; the next releases and market reactions remain unknown.
